question: Which food nutrient is mainly responsible for body building and fighting off infections?

options.A: Carbohydrates
options.B: Triglycerides
options.C: Simple sugars
options.D: Proteins

explanation: Great job! Proteins are made of amino acids, which act like the bricks and mortar of the body for repair, growth, and strong immunity. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T003#GNS227_U1_T003_h2)

question: Which measure should a clinic use when planning long-term care resources for people living with HIV?

options.A: Incidence
options.B: Fatality
options.C: Prevalence
options.D: Mortality

explanation: To know how many resources (like drugs and counseling space) are needed overall, you need prevalence—the total count of everyone living with the condition right now. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T86#GNS214_U1_T86_h3)

question: Which of these actions does NOT support safe patient care by a nurse leader?

options.A: Maintaining adequate staffing levels for patient acuity
options.B: Ensuring evidence-based clinical guidelines are followed
options.C: Punishing staff publicly for reporting near-misses
options.D: Promoting open communication and incident reporting

explanation: Spot on! Publicly punishing staff for speaking up only creates fear, making people hide their mistakes and putting patients at greater risk. [learn more](GST321_U3_T1#GST321_U3_T1_h7)

question: What is the main building block the body uses to make steroid hormones?

options.A: Glucose
options.B: Tyrosine
options.C: Cholesterol
options.D: Hemoglobin

explanation: Not all cholesterol is bad! Your body actually uses it as the foundational raw material to build important steroid hormones. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T1#GNS222_U2_T1_h3)

question: Why should nurses pay close attention to the worries of hospitalized patients?

options.A: It allows the nurse to shorten the visiting hours for relatives
options.B: It guarantees that the patient will pay their medical bills on time
options.C: Patients prefer strict institutional schedules over personal freedom
options.D: Fear and powerlessness can negatively impact healing and compliance

explanation: Well thought out! When patients are too stressed or scared, it can actually slow down their physical recovery and make them less likely to follow treatment. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T3#GNS112_U2_T3_h3)

question: What unusual sign might a patient on long-term steroids show when they catch an infection?

options.A: Low-grade fever
options.B: Rapid pus formation
options.C: Extreme high fever
options.D: Severe joint swelling

explanation: Because steroids quiet down the immune system, classic loud warning signs like a blazing high fever or heavy swelling might be hidden. A low-grade fever might be all you see! [learn more](GNS223_U7_T4#GNS223_U7_T4_h6)

question: Why are deworming tablets often given alongside school feeding programs?

options.A: Intestinal worms cause nutrient loss and anemia in children
options.B: Deworming tablets sweeten the drinking water supply
options.C: Parasites are required to help digest school meals properly
options.D: Worms prevent children from catching common cold viruses

explanation: Spot on! Worms steal important nutrients right from a child's tummy, which can cause malnutrition even if they eat good food. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T45#GNS214_U1_T45_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT one of the four legal elements needed to prove professional negligence?

options.A: Actual damages suffered by the patient
options.B: Direct causation of an injury
options.C: Guaranteed hospital bankruptcy
options.D: Breach of the legal duty of care

explanation: You got it! Hospital bankruptcy is just a financial state—it has nothing to do with the legal checklist needed to prove negligence in court. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T13#GNS125_U2_T13_h6)

question: How does water mostly travel across the lining of the large intestine?

options.A: Pumping uphill against concentration gradients
options.B: Evaporating through the abdominal wall
options.C: Following active sodium transport passively
options.D: Being pushed by direct muscular contractions

explanation: Water loves to follow salt! As the gut actively pumps sodium across its lining, water follows it smoothly through osmosis. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T4#GNS121_U1_T4_h6)

question: Which condition makes the rectal route unsafe because of a high risk of bleeding?

options.A: Mild tension headache
options.B: Simple upper respiratory infection
options.C: Severe thrombocytopenia
options.D: Chronic ankle swelling

explanation: Low platelet counts mean any trauma to the rectal lining can lead to serious, hard-to-stop bleeding. You've got this! [learn more](GNS122_U1_T5#GNS122_U1_T5_h2)

question: Why are accurate health records so important in busy primary health care clinics?

options.A: They ensure continuity of care when different health workers see the same patient over time.
options.B: They are used to calculate monthly staff salaries.
options.C: They replace physical exams when the clinic is crowded.
options.D: They guarantee the clinic gets international donor funds.

explanation: Patients often see different nurses on different days. Good records ensure the next nurse knows exactly what treatment was given, keeping the patient safe and cared for smoothly! [learn more](GNS124_U6_T2#GNS124_U6_T2_h1)

question: Why must community nurses look beyond the clinic when dealing with poor nutrition?

options.A: Because nutrition problems only exist inside large hospital wards
options.B: Because hospital management forbids nurses from talking about food
options.C: Because clinical medications can cure malnutrition completely on their own
options.D: Because root causes like poverty and food disruption require community-based action

explanation: Spot on! Nutritional challenges are often tied to bigger social and economic issues. Giving medicine alone isn't enough—we need community action and education too. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T17#GNS214_U1_T17_h1)

question: What is the normal, healthy pH range for human arterial blood?
explanation: Blood pH is tightly guarded between 7.35 and 7.45. Even a tiny shift outside this window can make a patient very sick, so the body works hard to protect it. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T13#GNS121_U2_T13_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a non-motor function linked to the cerebellum?

options.A: Language and word retrieval
options.B: Emotional mood modulation
options.C: Primary visual perception
options.D: Working memory and planning

explanation: Primary vision is handled in the occipital lobe at the back of the brain, not the cerebellum (though the cerebellum helps track eye movements!). You're crushing these questions. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T22#GNS211_U3_T22_h5)

question: What is the defining trait of "vulnerable populations" in community health?

options.A: They experience disproportionate health risks due to disadvantages
options.B: They always have direct access to private health insurance
options.C: They live exclusively in affluent urban neighborhoods
options.D: They hold leadership positions in local government

explanation: Spot on. These are groups who face extra health hurdles because of social, economic, or political disadvantages. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T2#GNS225_U1_T2_h6)

question: What is the main difference between monitoring and evaluation in public health projects?

options.A: Monitoring costs a lot of money, while evaluation is completely free
options.B: Monitoring is done only by doctors, while evaluation is done by patients
options.C: Monitoring is continuous tracking, while evaluation measures final outcomes against objectives
options.D: Monitoring focuses on finance, while evaluation focuses entirely on building roads

explanation: Monitoring happens all through the project to keep things on track, whereas evaluation looks back to see if goals were met. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h9)

question: Why do pregnant women often get painful muscle cramps in their legs at night?

options.A: The heavy uterus slows down blood return from the lower limbs.
options.B: Walking too much causes permanent nerve damage in the feet.
options.C: The thyroid gland stops functioning normally during sleep.
options.D: Excess calcium builds up rapidly in the calf muscles.

explanation: The growing uterus puts a bit of pressure on blood vessels in the pelvis, which can slow down circulation and lead to those annoying calf cramps. Staying hydrated helps! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T014#GNS226_U2_T014_h2)

question: What is the clock-face method used for during mealtime assistance?

options.A: Measuring the exact caloric content of each food portion
options.B: Describing the spatial location of food items on a plate
options.C: Checking the temperature of hot liquids before serving
options.D: Timing how fast the patient finishes eating their meal

explanation: The clock-face method (e.g., 'your rice is at 6 o'clock and chicken at 12 o'clock') helps visually impaired patients locate their food and eat independently. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T8#GNS324_U4_T8_h7)

question: Which of the following is a common management challenge in day care centres?

options.A: Complete absence of any government regulations
options.B: Too much space for very few enrolled children
options.C: High staff turnover and inadequate funding
options.D: Excessive numbers of trained medical doctors on site

explanation: Many day care centres struggle with financial constraints and frequent changes in caregiving staff, which can disrupt service quality. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h7)

question: What is the main goal of public health surveillance for nurses?

options.A: To manufacture vaccines in community health clinics
options.B: To punish hospitals that fail to report patient admissions
options.C: To prescribe antibiotics without a doctor's order
options.D: To systematically collect and analyze health data for disease trends

explanation: Surveillance keeps a close eye on disease patterns so we can catch outbreaks early and track down where germs are hiding. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T3#GNS313_U2_T3_h7)

question: About how much urine in an adult's bladder usually triggers the very first urge to go?

options.A: 1,500 to 2,000 milliliters
options.B: 3,000 to 4,000 milliliters
options.C: 200 to 400 milliliters
options.D: 10 to 20 milliliters

explanation: That's right! Around 200 to 400 ml of urine stretches the bladder enough to send those early 'time to pee' signals to your brain. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T9#GNS121_U2_T9_h4)

question: Which activity must occur before an HIV test is administered to a client?

options.A: Pre-test counselling
options.B: Public community notification
options.C: Mandatory partner isolation
options.D: Immediate antiretroviral drug loading

explanation: Pre-test counselling prepares the client mentally and ensures they understand the testing process and their rights. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T8#GNS216_U6_T8_h2)

question: Where do most traditional food beliefs and taboos originally come from?

options.A: From ancient survival experiences and local observations
options.B: From strict international food safety laws
options.C: From textbooks written by professional dietitians
options.D: From modern laboratory experiments conducted by scientists

explanation: Many food rules started long ago as clever ways to protect people from perceived dangers or explain natural events. History and culture run deep in our communities! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T017#GNS227_U2_T017_h2)

question: Why is late or messy clinical documentation a major legal risk for nurses?

options.A: Patients can read nurse notes and sue immediately for poor handwriting
options.B: Incomplete electronic records automatically trigger a state board license suspension
options.C: Hospital management uses missing notes as a reason to withhold holiday pay
options.D: Poor charting makes it difficult to prove that appropriate care and monitoring were actually provided

explanation: In nursing, the golden rule is: if it wasn't charted, it wasn't done! Clear notes are your best legal protection. [learn more](GST322_U4_T9#GST322_U4_T9_h4)

question: Which drug is given immediately for a patient experiencing severe anaphylactic shock?

options.A: Furosemide
options.B: Paracetamol
options.C: Epinephrine
options.D: Insulin

explanation: Epinephrine given in the muscle acts fast to open up airways and reverse dangerous swelling and drops in blood pressure. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T13#GNS321_U2_T13_h4)

question: What is a common long-term result of poor eating habits within a family?

options.A: Guaranteed immunity against all infectious diseases.
options.B: Chronic malnutrition and developmental stunting in children.
options.C: Immediate improvement in community economic status.
options.D: Increased agricultural crop yields for the next season.

explanation: You got it! Consistently missing out on key nutrients prevents growing children from reaching their full physical and mental potential. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T031#GNS227_U2_T031_h7)

question: Why are joints so important for our everyday movements?

options.A: They allow the rigid skeleton to move and bend
options.B: They connect skeletal muscles directly to other muscles
options.C: They produce all the red blood cells in the body
options.D: They store calcium and phosphorus for bone strength

explanation: Spot on! Without joints, our skeleton would be totally stiff. They give us the flexibility to walk, sit, and move around easily every day. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T5#GNS121_U3_T5_h1)

question: What are two major health issues strongly linked with a high BMI in the obesity range?

options.A: Hyperthyroidism and rapid muscle growth
options.B: Osteoporosis and iron deficiency anemia
options.C: Type 2 diabetes and hypertension
options.D: Insomnia and chronic low blood pressure

explanation: Correct! Carrying extra weight puts extra strain on the body's systems, making conditions like type 2 diabetes and high blood pressure much more likely. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T10#GNS121_U1_T10_h6)

question: Tracking a patient's fluid intake and output mainly helps you evaluate what?

options.A: Lung capacity and oxygen levels
options.B: Muscle strength in the lower limbs
options.C: Kidney function and hydration status
options.D: The patient's daily calorie intake

explanation: Checking what goes in versus what comes out is a brilliant way to see if the kidneys are doing their job and if the patient is well-hydrated. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T15#GNS212_U1_T15_h4)

question: What is a normal, expected feeling for a patient right after a sigmoidoscopy?

options.A: Mild belly bloating and the need to pass gas
options.B: Severe, sharp pain all over the stomach
options.C: Total numbness in both legs
options.D: An inability to pee for 24 hours

explanation: That's right! The air pumped into the bowel during the test has to come out somehow, causing temporary gas and bloating. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T6#GNS221_U2_T6_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of using a bowel diary for a patient with incontinence?

options.A: To test the chemical pH of passing stool
options.B: To track patterns of leakage, food intake, and bowel movements
options.C: To measure the exact length of the large intestine
options.D: To replace the need for a physical examination

explanation: A bowel diary provides concrete daily records of when and why accidents happen, helping nurses and doctors plan targeted interventions. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T8#GNS212_U1_T8_h5)

question: What is the primary reason why cleaning must happen before sterilization?

options.A: Organic matter protects germs from the sterilization process
options.B: Water makes the instruments softer to handle
options.C: Soap adds a layer of chemical protection
options.D: Washing removes the unpleasant metal smell

explanation: Dried blood and body fluids form a barrier over microorganisms that blocks heat or chemicals from reaching them. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a good way to prevent leaving items inside a patient?

options.A: Rushing through the final count to finish quickly
options.B: Using standardized hospital safety checklists
options.C: Minimizing operating room noise during counts
options.D: Encouraging open communication among staff

explanation: Never rush a count! Taking your time, staying calm, and keeping the room quiet helps catch errors. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T7#GNS123_U5_T7_h7)

question: Which of these is an example of secondary data during a community assessment?

options.A: Focus group discussions with village youths
options.B: Interviews conducted with mothers at the market
options.C: Existing clinic registers and census reports
options.D: Direct observation of village water sources

explanation: Correct! Secondary data is information that's already gathered and sitting there waiting for you, like old hospital records and government census books. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T2#GNS124_U3_T2_h5)

question: Why do people with substance addiction need higher doses over time to feel the same high?

options.A: The stomach lining thickens and stops absorbing the substance
options.B: The kidneys begin excreting the chemical before it reaches the brain
options.C: The liver starts producing extra enzymes that clear the drug too fast
options.D: The brain reduces its receptor sensitivity and natural chemical production

explanation: This is called tolerance! The brain tries to protect itself from excess drugs by cutting back on its own receptors and natural feel-good chemicals. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T11#GNS125_U2_T11_h4)

question: What is the main focus of a nurse's day-to-day role in neurological care?

options.A: Diagnosing rare genetic disorders independently
options.B: Performing complex brain surgery in the theater
options.C: Prescribing long-term neurological medications
options.D: Protecting delicate brain and nerve tissue from further damage

explanation: You are on the front lines! Nurses play a vital role in preventing nervous system damage and protecting neural tissue before any permanent harm can happen. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T24#GNS222_U3_T24_h1)

question: How should a nurse respond when community members attribute mental illness to spiritual causes?

options.A: Refuse to treat anyone in that community
options.B: Agree that hospitals are useless and refer everyone to shrines
options.C: Mock their beliefs and insist only on Western medicine
options.D: Acknowledge their perspective while respectfully integrating mental health education

explanation: Respecting local worldviews builds trust, allowing nurses to gently introduce helpful mental health concepts alongside traditional beliefs. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T7#GNS314_U4_T7_h5)

question: How often should a bedbound patient be turned to help prevent pressure injuries?

options.A: Only when requested
options.B: Every two hours
options.C: Once every shift
options.D: Every four hours

explanation: Turning a bedbound patient at least every two hours relieves pressure on bony prominences and restores blood flow to vulnerable tissues. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T9#GNS225_U5_T9_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of tertiary prevention in nursing care?

options.A: Preventing complications in established chronic diseases
options.B: Curing genetic disorders before birth
options.C: Stopping healthy people from ever getting sick
options.D: Screening asymptomatic populations for hidden risk

explanation: Well done! Tertiary prevention steps in after a diagnosis to help patients manage their condition and avoid further complications. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T17#GNS222_U2_T17_h4)

question: A school suddenly reports many students down with waterborne gastroenteritis. Which management duty failed here?

options.A: Provision of infrastructure and clean water
options.B: Budget allocation for sports equipment
options.C: Teacher salary negotiations
options.D: Curriculum integration for health education

explanation: Spot on. Waterborne illnesses are a clear warning sign that safe drinking water and proper sanitation need urgent attention. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T4#GNS225_U4_T4_h3)

question: Why must a nursing operational plan be kept simple?

options.A: So that every member of the healthcare team can easily understand and follow it.
options.B: So managers do not have to explain the plan during meetings.
options.C: Because complex medical terms confuse hospital accountants.
options.D: To make sure the planning document fits onto a single page.

explanation: If a plan is overly complicated, busy nurses and staff will misunderstand the steps. Simple plans keep everyone on the same page! [learn more](GST321_U1_T7#GST321_U1_T7_h2)

question: Why is the newborn wrapped in a clean cloth right after birth?

options.A: To absorb excess amniotic fluid for testing
options.B: To protect the baby from bright room lights
options.C: To stimulate deep breathing reflexes
options.D: To prevent heat loss and hypothermia

explanation: Newborns lose body heat very quickly through evaporation and environmental exposure, making prompt drying and wrapping essential. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T10#GNS225_U2_T10_h4)

question: What is the main difference between parenteral (injectable) and oral anticoagulants?

options.A: Parenteral agents are injected for fast action, while oral agents are swallowed for long-term use
options.B: Parenteral drugs only target platelets, while oral drugs target the whole clotting cascade
options.C: Oral medications are only used in emergency intensive care units
options.D: Oral agents never require lab tests, whereas parenteral drugs need daily blood checks

explanation: You got it! When we need a fast response in an emergency, we inject it (parenteral). For long-term home use, pills (oral) are much easier for patients. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T5#GNS223_U1_T5_h2)

question: Which sign strongly suggests a patient is struggling to swallow during a meal?

options.A: Asking for a glass of clean water
options.B: Finishing the meal within ten minutes
options.C: A gurgling voice right after swallowing
options.D: Chewing food slowly on one side

explanation: Spot on! A wet or gurgling voice means food or drink slipped into the upper airway. Good eye spotting that! [learn more](GNS324_U3_T7#GNS324_U3_T7_h4)

question: How can clinical nurses take part in disaster prevention?

options.A: Managing the national budget for emergency services
options.B: Educating patients on protecting vital medicines during power cuts
options.C: Passing national laws that restrict building near riverbanks
options.D: Designing heavy structural blueprints for new hospitals

explanation: Fantastic! Nurses help patients prepare by teaching them how to manage their health when emergencies happen. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T11#GNS315_U5_T11_h6)

question: A community nurse is teaching rural farmers how to avoid hookworm. What is the best practical advice to share?

options.A: Wear protective footwear consistently when working outdoors
options.B: Avoid eating raw vegetables harvested from flooded river valleys
options.C: Take prophylactic antibiotics every morning before breakfast
options.D: Boil all drinking water for at least two hours before consumption

explanation: Since hookworm larvae wait in the soil to burrow through bare skin, putting on footwear is a simple, life-saving habit for farmers. [learn more](GST114_U3_T6#GST114_U3_T6_h8)

question: Why do patients still need supportive care (like IV fluids and oxygen) even after getting an antidote?

options.A: Antidotes usually worsen the patient's baseline vital signs
options.B: Supportive care keeps the patient stable while the body handles the toxin
options.C: Supportive care replaces the need for any toxicological screening
options.D: Antidotes are completely ineffective without continuous intravenous fluids

explanation: Antidotes are amazing, but they aren't instant magic. Supportive care keeps the patient breathing and stable while the antidote and the body do the heavy lifting to clear the poison. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T7#GNS215_U5_T7_h1)

question: Where does the body store extra energy once glycogen reserves are completely full?

options.A: Adipose tissue as triglycerides
options.B: Inside the renal tubules
options.C: Inside the central nervous system
options.D: Directly within the bloodstream

explanation: Spot on! When your quick-storage tanks (glycogen) are packed, the body neatly converts the extra energy into fat for storage in adipose tissue. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T013#GNS227_U1_T013_h5)

question: Which set of symptoms in a postpartum mother is a strong warning sign of impending eclampsia (seizures)?

options.A: Severe headache, blurred vision, and upper tummy (epigastric) pain
options.B: Dry mouth, joint stiffness, and mild fatigue
options.C: Frequent urination, extreme thirst, and itchy skin
options.D: Cough, chest pain, and difficulty breathing

explanation: Keep your eyes open for these head and tummy warning signs! They tell you severe pre-eclampsia might be progressing into dangerous seizures. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T022#GNS226_U3_T022_h3)

question: Why is it risky for a nursing research project to lack clear objectives?

options.A: The study will easily lose direction and gather irrelevant data
options.B: The nursing staff will refuse to participate in the study
options.C: The sample size will become too large to calculate
options.D: The hospital ethics committee will automatically grant funding

explanation: Without clear targets, you might end up collecting a mountain of unnecessary information that doesn't actually solve your clinical problem. Good objectives keep you focused! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T9#GNS217_U3_T9_h1)

question: Why do nurses take a baseline set of vital signs when a patient is first admitted?

options.A: To diagnose chronic illnesses right away
options.B: To establish a starting point for future comparisons
options.C: To replace the need for a physical exam
options.D: To figure out the exact date of discharge

explanation: Spot on! Baseline values give you a clear reference point so you can easily track whether your patient is getting better or worse over time. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T4#GNS123_U2_T4_h1)

question: Roughly how many half-lives does it take for a stopped medication to be almost completely cleared from the body?

options.A: 1 to 2 half-lives
options.B: 10 to 12 half-lives
options.C: 4 to 5 half-lives
options.D: 20 to 24 half-lives

explanation: As a rule of thumb, after about 4 to 5 half-lives, less than 5% of the drug is left. Clinically, we consider the drug completely washed out by then! [learn more](GNS125_U1_T4#GNS125_U1_T4_h6)

question: Why is an injury high up on the spinal cord considered a major medical emergency?

options.A: It stops the digestive system from absorbing water
options.B: It automatically causes complete memory loss
options.C: It can paralyze the muscles needed for breathing
options.D: It prevents the heart from producing blood cells

explanation: That's right! High cervical injuries cut off nerve signals to the diaphragm and chest, making it hard or impossible for the patient to breathe on their own without quick support. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T13#GNS222_U3_T13_h3)

question: What happens to bacteria when food is placed inside a properly working freezer?

options.A: They are instantly and fully killed.
options.B: Their reproduction stops completely.
options.C: They multiply faster in the cold air.
options.D: They turn into spores and fly away.

explanation: Freezing puts bacteria to sleep (dormant state), stopping them from multiplying, but it doesn't kill them completely. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T012#GNS227_U3_T012_h5)

question: During a home visit, what is a key sign of neglect that a community health nurse should look for?

options.A: Frequent attendance at youth club meetings
options.B: A high grade point average in primary school
options.C: Poor hygiene and delayed physical growth milestones
options.D: Excessive participation in neighborhood sports

explanation: Physical signs like poor hygiene and stunted growth point directly to a lack of proper care, food, and supervision at home. Excellent assessment skill to master! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T2#GNS225_U5_T2_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of a community health monitoring framework?

options.A: To replace traditional bedside nursing documentation with digital spreadsheets
options.B: To serve as a blueprint guiding data flow, collection responsibilities, and reporting schedules
options.C: To secure permanent international funding without local community input
options.D: To punish health workers who fail to meet their monthly targets

explanation: Think of a monitoring framework as your roadmap—it guides everyone on what to measure, when to report, and who is in charge. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T21#GNS225_U2_T21_h4)

question: Why must a patient keep their affected leg straight and flat after a femoral EPS?

options.A: To prevent bleeding and hematoma formation at the vascular access site
options.B: To allow the newly mapped heart chambers to settle into position
options.C: To ensure the patient stays awake during the recovery phase
options.D: To help the local anesthesia wear off faster in the leg muscles

explanation: Bending that leg right after a catheter goes into the groin artery is a recipe for bleeding. Keeping it straight protects the clot so the puncture can heal safely! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T10#GNS222_U3_T10_h5)

question: At 34 weeks, an antenatal patient is found to have a soft heart murmur. What should the midwife do first?

options.A: Immediately send the patient to the emergency operating theatre
options.B: Recognize it as a common normal finding due to increased blood volume
options.C: Order emergency blood transfusions to correct severe anemia
options.D: Diagnose the patient with permanent rheumatic heart disease

explanation: Brilliant! Extra blood flow and heart position changes often cause harmless murmurs during pregnancy. No need to panic! [learn more](GNS121_U7_T2#GNS121_U7_T2_h8)

question: How do bile salts help your body digest fats?

options.A: Breaking large fat globules into tiny emulsified droplets
options.B: Releasing digestive enzymes directly into the fat droplets
options.C: Neutralizing stomach acid before fats reach the intestine
options.D: Chemically dissolving fats into simple fatty acids

explanation: Bile salts act just like dish soap, turning big globs of fat into tiny droplets so digestive enzymes can easily reach them. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T11#GNS121_U1_T11_h5)

question: Why is a change in mental status often the first sign of developing shock?

options.A: Brain tissue is extremely sensitive to reductions in oxygen and blood supply
options.B: Fluid overload in the bloodstream causes immediate brain swelling
options.C: Pain receptors in the skin send distress signals to the brain
options.D: Anxiety releases hormones that directly cause kidney failure

explanation: The brain has high metabolic demands and reacts quickly when oxygen delivery drops, making confusion or restlessness an early alarm bell. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T5#GNS123_U3_T5_h6)

question: Which viral infection is known as the main cause of cervical cancer?

options.A: Hepatitis B Virus
options.B: Human Papillomavirus
options.C: Human Immunodeficiency Virus
options.D: Herpes Simplex Virus

question: Why is it important for nurses to know the difference between the incubation period and the latent period?

question: Why is goal congruence beneficial for a healthcare facility?

question: What is the biggest benefit of working hand-in-hand with local leaders during health campaigns?

question: What is the most common cause of peripheral neuropathy worldwide?

question: Who starts the whole disease-reporting chain right at the grassroots level?

question: Why is the cerebral aqueduct considered a high-risk spot for fluid blockage?

question: What is the primary focus of dietary counselling?

question: What main factor sets gender-based violence apart from other forms of violence?

question: What is the main feature of self-directed violence?

question: What is the best way to talk to a patient who has trouble communicating after a stroke?

options.A: Always finish their sentences if they take longer than two seconds

question: When does the assessment of a patient's mental status actually begin?

question: Why is it important to gather all your IV equipment before you walk to the patient's bedside?

question: What was a major focus of early public health pioneers like Florence Nightingale?

question: An elderly patient taking a first-generation antihistamine for itching complains they can't pass urine easily. What's the likely culprit?

options.C: Anticholinergic side effects causing urinary retention
options.D: An undiagnosed urinary tract infection from the allergy

question: What happens to bile between meals when your body doesn't need it right away?

options.B: It is broken down into simple sugars by liver enzymes
options.C: It is stored and concentrated inside the gallbladder
options.D: It is sent back to the stomach to digest proteins

question: Which of the following is a classic example of a prerenal cause of acute kidney injury?

options.C: A large kidney stone blocking the ureter completely

question: What is the term for an infection that jumps naturally between animals and humans?

options.A: Nosocomial infection

question: What should a nurse tell a patient to expect regarding bleeding after taking these medications?

options.B: Expect only light spotting that stops entirely within two hours

question: Why must a patient wait nearly three months to check if lifestyle changes improved his sperm count?

question: Which type of FGM involves cutting and repositioning the labia to create a covering seal over the vaginal opening?

question: A patient who lost both legs in a car accident last week is angry and crying over lost independence. How would you classify this response?

question: Why do nurses commonly use compresses in the ward?

question: Why is it important to involve local community assets during resource mobilization?

options.A: Government policy forbids spending money on outside contractors

question: Why is independent double-checking required for medications like insulin and heparin?

question: Which major international conference linked population policy directly with human rights?

question: A clinic ensures that its facility can be reached easily by rural women and has fair pricing. Which core dimension is being prioritized?

question: Why do foetal lungs get only a tiny fraction of the body's blood supply?

question: Why do babies need other foods (complementary feeding) introduced around six months of age?

question: What is the main purpose of contact tracing during an infectious disease outbreak?

question: A poorly nourished child living in a crowded area comes down with frequent infections. Which factor is most responsible for lowering this child's defenses?

question: Why might a patient with a cyst test negative on a routine antibody blood test?

question: What is the main job of progesterone during the female reproductive cycle?

question: An HIV-positive mum asks if she can give her two-month-old baby sips of plain water during hot weather. What is your best response as a nurse?

question: What is the main purpose of the ductus arteriosus in a foetus?

question: What is the number one symptom patients with vulval inflammation usually report?

question: A community experiences a sudden outbreak of severe diarrhea linked to contaminated street food. What is the most appropriate regulatory response?

explanation: Makes sense, right? We use our hands and lips for detailed tasks, so they need way more brain power and receptor coverage than our backs! [learn more](GNS211_U4_T11#GNS211_U4_T11_h6)

question: During an IV insertion, what lets you know for sure that your needle has successfully entered the vein?

options.A: The infusion bag begins to drip rapidly without any pressure.
options.B: The surrounding skin turns pale and cool to the touch.
options.C: The patient reports a sudden cooling sensation in the arm.
options.D: A flash of blood appears inside the flashback chamber of the device.

explanation: That's right! Seeing that little 'flash' of dark red blood in the chamber is the classic sign that you're in the vein. Beautiful work! [learn more](GNS311_U4_T6#GNS311_U4_T6_h5)

question: Which cells in the pancreas are responsible for producing insulin?

options.A: Alpha cells
options.B: Beta cells
options.C: Delta cells
options.D: Acinar cells

explanation: Insulin is synthesized and secreted by the beta cells located within the islets of Langerhans in the pancreas. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T17#GNS324_U4_T17_h1)

question: When should you definitely NOT use an alcohol-based hand rub?

options.A: When hands are visibly dirty or soiled with body fluids
options.B: Between examining two different patients
options.C: After touching a clean bedside table
options.D: Before entering a patient room for a vital signs check

explanation: If your hands have visible dirt or body fluids on them, alcohol won't cut through it. Head to the sink for soap and water instead! [learn more](GST114_U2_T6#GST114_U2_T6_h7)

question: Which hormone acts like the body's main thermostat for controlling metabolism?

options.A: Insulin
options.B: Thyroxine
options.C: Melatonin
options.D: Oxytocin

explanation: Thyroxine, made by the thyroid gland, sets the speed at which your cells turn nutrients into energy and heat. Great hormone to remember for your exams! [learn more](GNS227_U1_T014#GNS227_U1_T014_h3)

question: Why are good learning experiences so important for you as a nursing student?

options.A: They eliminate the need for any written nursing examinations
options.B: They help connect classroom theory to real patient care realities
options.C: They shorten the overall duration of the nursing training program
options.D: They guarantee that students never make clinical errors on the ward

explanation: They bridge the gap between what you read in your textbooks and what you actually see and do at the bedside. Great for building your confidence! [learn more](GST321_U8_T5#GST321_U8_T5_h1)

question: A breastfeeding mother who delivered six weeks ago asks for a contraceptive implant. What should you tell her?

options.A: She must first undergo a liver biopsy to prove her body can tolerate the progestin hormone
options.B: She is completely ineligible because implants will immediately dry up her breast milk supply
options.C: She is eligible, as progestin-only implants do not interfere with milk production and are safe during breastfeeding
options.D: She must wait until her baby is at least one year old before any hormonal method can be discussed

explanation: Great news for new mums! Progestin-only options are safe during breastfeeding and won't mess with her milk supply. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T014#GNS226_U6_T014_h4)

question: What kind of lubricant should you put on the tip of an NG tube before sliding it in?

options.A: Water-soluble lubricant
options.B: Petroleum jelly base
options.C: Alcohol-based gel
options.D: Sterile mineral oil

explanation: Always use a water-soluble jelly! If a tiny bit accidentally goes into the lungs, the body absorbs it safely without causing nasty lung issues. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T1#GNS212_U1_T1_h3)

question: During the final delivery of the baby's body, which part usually comes out first?

options.A: The posterior hip
options.B: The umbilical cord
options.C: The anterior shoulder
options.D: The lower extremities

explanation: Spot on! The front shoulder slips out from under the pubic bone first, and then the back shoulder follows. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h7)

question: What key lesson did the world learn from successful global vaccination campaigns against smallpox?

options.A: Coordinated international public health strategies can eradicate major diseases
options.B: Vaccines are only effective inside sterile hospital operating rooms
options.C: Local communities cannot participate in disease prevention
options.D: Infectious diseases disappear naturally without human intervention

explanation: Teamwork works! Smallpox proved that when the whole world joins forces on immunization, we can wipe out deadly diseases. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T6#GNS225_U2_T6_h5)
